Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm 76, been farming this little patch for 50 years, so I know it well. It's just me and the old lady at home now — the kids all went to the city long ago. 4.1 mu isn't much but it's enough to keep us fed and give us a little cash.

I'll split the land like I always do: about 2 mu for the wheat-maize rotation on the better plot, and 2.1 mu for cotton on the western plot — that soil doesn't hold water as well, and cotton does alright there. I've tried switching it all to wheat-maize before, but cotton still brings in some cash at the end of the year, and my wife and I can manage the picking if we take our time. For the heavy work I'll pay the neighbor's son with the tractor and the combine — can't swing a hoe all day at my age.

**Wheat (about 2 mu):** I'll plant in mid-October after the maize comes off, same as always. Use the Jimai variety seed I bought at the agri-supply shop — I don't save my own anymore, the hybrid stuff does better. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, maybe 40 kg/mu of the 15-15-15 stuff, that's around 6 kg of N up front. Then when it greens up in spring around jointing, I topdress urea, maybe 15 kg/mu — the extension guy said less but I've always done it this way and the wheat looks good. Irrigate at planting, then greening water in spring, then at jointing, and once more at grain filling if it's dry. Four times usually. Spray herbicide once in spring for the weeds, that's all.

**Maize (same 2 mu, after wheat):** Tight window — I get the combine through for wheat harvest on June 10th or so, then the neighbor's boy comes with the no-till planter the next day or two. Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid seed is in stock. Fertilizer goes down with the planter, compound 15-15-15 about 30 kg/mu. If the maize looks pale at the big-trumpet stage I'll topdress another 10 kg of urea. Usually don't irrigate unless July is dry. Spray for armyworm if I see them. Harvest end of September.

**Cotton (2.1 mu):** This is the one that takes the most out of me. Plow and bed up in April, plant mid-April when the soil is warm. I buy the Bt cotton seed — no choice these days, can't fight the bollworm otherwise. Base fertilizer compound about 30 kg/mu before planting, then topdress urea 8 kg/mu at squaring and another 8 kg at flowering. Irrigate once or twice in July-August if it's hot and dry. Spray pesticide a few times for aphids and spider mites. The picking — that's me and the old lady, goes on from September into October, three or four passes. We're slow but we get it done.

Money is tight — pensions are small, our son sends a bit but not much. So I don't go crazy on inputs. Same routine as last year, last year was okay.
